text:
Viktor Arvidsson is 33, on his fifth NHL team, and in his first season in Detroit he is still doing what he has always done: getting to the front of the net. He has 9.98 expected goals (the quality of his chances), 1.54 per 60 minutes, above the rate he posted last season.

The results have stalled. He opened with a hat trick against Chicago on Oct. 29 and then went eight games without a goal on 2.5 expected, which our numbers call due. Over the same stretch he has gone six without a point, and there the chances have thinned. Overall, 8 goals on 10.0 expected leaves him about two short, and Detroit has scored 3.4 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 9.2 slot chances per 60 last season, 99th percentile among forwards, and carrying the puck in on 58% of entries. Octopus Thrower wrote that "The numbers back up Viktor Arvidsson's stellar play." We agree on the chances. Watch whether the finishing catches up.
